scenarios.title: The Former Teammate's Retirement
scenarios.text: A teammate you've lined up beside for years retires on a Wednesday. Thursday morning his locker is empty, and the room sounds different.

choices.label: Keep in touch
choices.result: You keep in touch. He calls on game days with notes from his couch, and the calls get funnier the longer he's away.

choices.label: Fill the space
choices.result: You start doing the things he used to do: the jokes before meetings, the check-ins on rookies. It's harder than he made it look.

choices.label: Let it be different
choices.result: You let it be different. Rooms change; this one will too. You notice his empty chair less each week, and feel guilty about that.

scenarios.title: The New Contract Negotiation
scenarios.text: Your agent wants a longer deal, and the club wants a shorter one.

choices.label: Take the shorter deal
choices.result: You take the shorter deal and bet on yourself.

choices.label: Fight for the longer one
choices.result: You fight for the longer one. It takes a month.

choices.label: Talk to the club yourself
choices.result: You talk to the club yourself. You meet in the middle.

scenarios.title: The Media Debate
scenarios.text: On a sports show, two analysts spend ten minutes arguing about whether you're still among the best kickers in the league. Your phone fills with clips.

choices.label: Use it
choices.result: You watch it once and put the losing argument on a card in your locker. Every practice that week, you kick like you're answering it.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.result: You turn off the television and leave your phone in the car during practice. By Thursday the debate has moved on, and so have you.

choices.label: Laugh about it
choices.result: You laugh about it with the specialists, who do impressions of both analysts all week. It's the loosest the unit has been all year.

scenarios.title: The Community Commitment
scenarios.text: A local charity wants you as its face, year-round: the posters, the hospital visits, the winter coat drive. It's a real commitment.

choices.label: Commit
choices.result: You commit to the full year. It's a lot of evenings, and the coat drive breaks the city's record.

choices.label: Bring teammates
choices.result: You bring teammates so the work is shared. It becomes a team tradition, and the young players start signing up on their own.

choices.label: Do the big events
choices.result: You do the big events only. It helps, and you can tell the charity hoped for more.

scenarios.title: The Expensive Lifestyle
scenarios.text: Your household's expenses have quietly doubled.

choices.label: Cut back
choices.result: You sit down and cut back. Some things go, and nobody misses them.

choices.label: Talk to {love_interest}
choices.result: You talk to {love_interest}. You make a plan together.

choices.label: Let it ride
choices.result: You let it ride. You'll deal with it later.

scenarios.title: The Advisor's Concern
scenarios.text: Your financial advisor slides one line of your statement across the table and asks, carefully, whether you still want to be in it. It's the investment a teammate talked you into.

choices.label: Listen and adjust
choices.result: You listen, ask the questions you skipped the first time, and move most of the money out. It costs you a little, and you sleep better.

choices.label: Get a second opinion
choices.result: You show it to someone you trust before deciding. They read it twice, sigh, and explain the part you didn't understand. You get out together.

choices.label: Keep it
choices.result: You keep it. You like the idea and the teammate, and you tell yourself the advisor is just being careful. The statement keeps arriving.

scenarios.title: The Team Rebuild
scenarios.text: The club has started replacing veterans with younger, cheaper players. Every week another familiar locker is cleared out, and you've started counting.

choices.label: Stay ahead
choices.result: You get ahead of the clock: earlier mornings, cleaner numbers. If they want to replace you, they'll have to find someone better.

choices.label: Help the young players
choices.result: You help the young players learn the job. It's the right thing, and it makes you the veteran the club can't afford to lose.

choices.label: Talk to your agent
choices.result: You sit down with your agent and talk through the next two years honestly. It's a hard conversation, and a relief to have it.

scenarios.title: The New Special Teams Coach
scenarios.text: The new special teams coach stops a drill in front of the whole unit to ask why you still warm up the way you did as a rookie. Everyone is watching to see what you do.

choices.label: Answer with data
choices.result: You bring him three seasons of charts after practice, in his office, with the door closed. He reads every page and changes one drill, not yours.

choices.label: Answer with work
choices.result: You say nothing and out-work everyone for a week. He stops asking in public, though you can tell the question is still there.

choices.label: Talk to him alone
choices.result: You ask for ten minutes alone and tell him what the routine is for. He listens, and the next morning he warms up the young kicker your way.

scenarios.title: The Mentor's Retirement
scenarios.text: The special teams coach who rebuilt your swing in your second season is stepping away at the end of the year. He hasn't told the room yet; he told you first.

choices.label: Thank him
choices.result: You drive to his house on a Tuesday and thank him in his kitchen. He waves it off, then walks you to the car and doesn't let go of the handshake.

choices.label: Organize a send-off
choices.result: You call every kicker and punter he ever coached. Eleven of them show up for his last practice, and he has to turn around to the fence for a minute.

choices.label: Leave a note
choices.result: You write him a note and leave it in his playbook. He never mentions it, but on his last day it's the only thing he takes from the desk.

scenarios.title: The Old Rival
scenarios.text: A competitor from years ago reaches out out of nowhere.

choices.label: Meet for lunch
choices.result: You meet for lunch. It's warmer than you expected.

choices.label: Ask what he needs
choices.result: You ask what he needs. It's advice, and you give it.

choices.label: Reply politely
choices.result: You reply politely and leave it there.

scenarios.title: The Family Business Dispute
scenarios.text: A business with relatives in it is turning into a family fight.

choices.label: Bring in a mediator
choices.result: You bring in a mediator. It's expensive and it works.

choices.label: Step back
choices.result: You step back from the business and keep the family.

choices.label: Take charge
choices.result: You take charge. It's a lot of work, and a few people are mad.

scenarios.title: The College Invitation
scenarios.text: A university you never played for invites you to speak to its football program. The head coach says the kickers have been asking for you by name all spring.

choices.label: Speak to the team
choices.result: You give the team a short talk about failing in front of people. The kickers stay after and ask questions until the groundskeeper turns off the lights.

choices.label: Spend the day
choices.result: You spend the whole day: meetings, lunch, practice. By the end, a freshman kicker who barely spoke at breakfast is showing you his notebook.

choices.label: Send a video
choices.result: You send a video instead. It's thoughtful and it plays well, and you see later that the kickers watched it twice.

scenarios.title: The Team's Direction
scenarios.text: You're not sure the franchise is going in the right direction, and someone asks you on the record.

choices.label: Say something careful
choices.result: You say something careful and true. Fans respect it; the front office notices.

choices.label: Back the club
choices.result: You back the club publicly.

choices.label: Say it to the club
choices.result: You say it to the club, not the reporter.
